profile.heading: Your course profile in an AI-shaped world

measures.name: Working Alongside AI
measures.explanation: How strongly your course develops the ability to use AI productively alongside your own subject knowledge and judgement.
strengthenedBy: scope to use AI tools productively in the work the course leads to

measures.name: Human and Practical Capability
measures.explanation: How strongly the course develops capabilities involving people, judgement, practical activity and original thinking.

measures.name: Transferable Capability
measures.explanation: How widely the course develops capabilities that can transfer across different roles and settings.

profile.summary: The course gives you a moderate basis for working alongside AI tools. It places strong emphasis on work with people, judgement, practical activity and original thinking. Its capabilities appear to transfer to a moderate range of roles and settings.

perspectives.overall: Your course profile describes the course as you outlined it, measure by measure.
perspectives.aiLearning: AI may help you prepare, explore ideas and check your understanding as you study.
perspectives.humanPractical: Much of the course asks you to apply your own judgement and practical skill.
perspectives.transferable: The reasoning and communication you build here carry into many settings.
perspectives.actionPlanIntroduction: The plan below turns these findings into steps for now, the coming months and later study.

skills.title: Professional judgement and standards
skills.explanation: 7 of your 8 analysed modules appear shaped by professional or client-facing standards, such as Module 1 and Module 3. Applying those standards with your own judgement is a priority.

skills.title: Communication and collaboration
skills.explanation: 5 of your 8 analysed modules involve substantial work with other people, such as Module 1 and Module 4. Communication and collaboration are a priority.

skills.title: Critical evaluation and independent reasoning
skills.explanation: 4 of your 8 analysed modules centre on interpretation and judgement, such as Module 4 and Module 5. Building your own reasoning, and testing AI output against it, is a priority.

skills.title: Practical application
skills.explanation: 2 of your 8 analysed modules place weight on practical or hands-on work, such as Module 1 and Module 8. Developing that capability through practice and feedback is a priority.

skills.title: Technical and quantitative foundations
skills.explanation: 2 of your 8 analysed modules have a strong technical or quantitative core, such as Module 2 and Module 3. Secure foundations let you use AI tools well and check their technical output.

safeguards.title: Your own work in assessed modules
safeguards.text: In Module 1 and Module 8, AI may be useful for learning and preparation, but these modules strongly depend on demonstrating your own capability. Check your institution's assessment rules before using AI in assessed work.

safeguards.title: Professional and client-facing standards
safeguards.text: Module 1, Module 3, Module 4 and 4 other modules appear to involve professional, clinical or client-facing standards. Treat AI output as support rather than authority, and verify important conclusions against appropriate course or professional guidance.

safeguards.title: Checking AI-generated technical work
safeguards.text: When AI helps with calculations, code or technical reasoning in Module 2 and Module 3, check its working yourself: AI output can look correct and still be wrong.

safeguards.title: Checking AI-generated claims and sources
safeguards.text: When AI summarises reading or suggests claims, quotations or references for Module 4, Module 5, Module 6 and 1 other module, check them against the original sources before relying on them.

plan.title: Next 30 days
actions: Find the course or professional guidance that applies to Module 1, and keep it to hand as the reference you check AI output against.
Take one AI-generated summary or claim about your reading for Module 4 and check it against the original source, including any quotations or references.
Before your next practical session in Module 8, agree one skill to work on and how you will get feedback on it.
Pick the topic in Module 2 you find hardest and work on it without AI first, so you can judge AI explanations of it later.

plan.title: This term
actions: Compare one AI answer about Module 1 with your course or professional guidance, and note where they differ and which you would rely on.
Use group, client or patient-facing work in Module 1 to get feedback on how you communicate.
In Module 4, form and write down your own interpretation before you consult AI, then compare the two.
Ask for feedback on your practical work in Module 8, and act on one point before the next assessment.

plan.title: Next 6 to 12 months
actions: Look for placements, projects or volunteering that add further hands-on experience alongside Module 1 and Module 8.
Follow how professional guidance in your field treats AI use, and how it applies to work like Module 1.
Collect examples of decisions, interpretations or communication you handled yourself in Module 1, Module 4, Module 6 and 2 other modules, so you can describe your judgement to others.
Build a small portfolio of your own work from Module 1 and Module 8, showing your process as well as the result.

limitations: This report assesses the structure of the course and the module information supplied, not your own ability.
It is not a prediction of employment, job prospects or salary.
AI capabilities and university policies change, so some findings may date.
Always check your institution's and each module's assessment rules before using AI in assessed work.
External labour-market evidence is not part of this course profile or its measures.
